deployment.sourceEvidence: root-attested per-run manifests and deployment snapshots

result.continuityReason: Each run deliberately interrupts its Signal transport once; five successful recoveries are not an uninterrupted continuity qualification.

method.faultMeaning: The ordinary probe explicitly closes its current native Signal transport once; this does not directly exercise two missing heartbeat ACK deadlines.
method.restorePath: Existing authenticated Signal reconnect and formal Host viewer-session rebind, followed by required mouse and keyboard resets.
method.hostWindowSelection: Resource/queue windows: each deployment snapshot verification time through its first subsequent Signal viewer_disconnect_grace_expired event. Peer cleanup events additionally include a fixed 2000ms read-only observation tail so cleanup dispatched at the final boundary can settle; no probe gate or recovery deadline is changed.
method.hostSamplingLimit: Host resource/queue fields are sampled windows, not continuous proof of zero transient queue depth or zero resource cost.
method.crossClockLimit: Browser-derived UTC labels are provenance anchors only; no browser-to-Host wall-clock subtraction is used for latency metrics.

resetLatencyContract.aggregation: For each metric, retain the maximum reported rolling-window p95 across the five overlapping snapshots. Each window count is 2; current percentile implementation selects the larger of the two samples. These are per-run two-sample maxima, not whole-session or population p95 values.
resetLatencyContract.noSnapshotCountMultiplication: The five snapshots repeatedly observe the same two input associations; they are not ten independent inputs.
resetLatencyContract.inputAckRttMs: Viewer transport submission to its matching successful input ACK callback; includes transport, browser/Signal/Host scheduling and execution.
resetLatencyContract.inputToPostApplyFrameMs: Viewer submission to its same-scope matched RTP/SSRC video-frame callback carrying a fresh capture after successful application. Two inputs can share one presented frame. This is not evidence of application response content or physical display presentation.
resetLatencyContract.hostQueueMs: Host adapter-local monotonic nanoseconds from adapter queue boundary to native apply start, divided by 1000000.
resetLatencyContract.hostApplyMs: Host native apply interval in the same monotonic clock, divided by 1000000.
resetLatencyContract.hostAdapterAwaitMs: Host adapter entry through adapter return measured by perf_counter seconds times 1000; includes adapter-local queue time but excludes the outer Host admission wait.
forbiddenDerivations: Do not add metric p95 values; maxima may belong to different reset actions.
Do not subtract Host adapter duration from ACK RTT and label the remainder network latency.
Do not add ACK RTT and post-apply-frame duration; both start at the same Viewer submission.
Do not treat a frame callback as controlled visible effect.
Do not treat Host ACK enqueue as Viewer receipt; the separate Viewer ACK RTT metric provides the matched-receipt evidence here.
resetLatencyContract.frameBeforeAckIsAllowed: The matched post-apply video callback can precede the ACK callback because these observations arrive over different paths.

limitations: Five short ordinary recovery runs do not establish a 30-minute or three-hour uninterrupted session, a public-path latency SLO, or immunity to later natural disconnects.
The prior natural lease-expiry failure and the older single-timeout-watchdog baseline failure remain retained as failures; neither is counted as a pass here.
Only mandatory recovery reset actions were measured. Business mouse/keyboard actions, controlled marker visible effects and physical display latency were not run.
Browser lifecycle ring coverage is partial and drops older bounded events; counters and source summaries are retained, but a complete browser event history is unavailable.
Owned browser close API completion is known, while owned browser process exit was not observed; cleanup remains api-finished-exit-unknown.
Lease expiry and reset-only cleanup after the owned browser closes are expected teardown observations, not additional active-session recovery failures.
Signal accepted/ACK-enqueued summaries do not establish remote ACK delivery and must not be summed across repeated summary events.
